text:
Maria (runtime): quick run of the slab-recycler experiment on staging prefix-cache, posting summary + logs. wanted eyes on hit-rate vs fragmentation tradeoff.
AJ: nice — which config did you change exactly? slab size / free-list policy?
Maria (runtime): changed three things: lowered shard workspace cap to 32MB, enabled slab_recycler=true (recycles freed blocks within shard), and switched from LRU eviction to size-aware eviction for large prefixes.
Sam R: perf summary from the trace: peak GPU mem before = 88.1GB, after = 74.6GB (stable across 6 stress runs). overall hit-rate delta: -0.8% absolute (was 74.2% -> 73.4%). p95 token latency increased ~4ms on synthetic spikes.
PerfBot: experiment-id=e37f1, config=staging-slab-recycler-32mb, runs=6, peak_mem_gb=74.6, median_hitrate=73.4, median_latency_ms=12.7, p95_latency_ms=34.5
Eli: where is the fragmentation coming from? are we leaving many small holes that the allocator can't reuse across shards?
Maria (runtime): yes, fragmentation dropped by ~18% (heap stats), but recycler only works intra-shard. cross-shard fragmentation still present because slabs are pinned to shard owner.
AJ: could we try a shared free pool between shards? maybe allow cross-shard slab donations under low load?
Sam R: tried a naive donor pool in a micro-experiment: when shard free list > threshold, donate slab -> global pool. result: peak mem similar to recycler, hit-rate stayed flat, but observed contention spikes when pool drained -> p95 jitter increased.
Maria (runtime): logs snippet of allocator stats:

```
AllocatorStats: total_slabs=284, free_slabs=46, recycled_slabs=112, cross_shard_donations=8
FragmentationBefore=0.29, FragmentationAfter=0.11
ShardSizes: mean=4.75MB, median=2.1MB, large_prefix_count=312
```

Eli: that donation contention is worrying. maybe use async background scavenger to move slabs instead of sync donate on allocation path.
AJ: agree — background compaction + tail-latency guard might help. also curious about TTL effects: did you reduce TTLs when enabling recycler?
Maria (runtime): left TTL at 1h in this run. lowering TTL to 10m will reduce memory but may reduce hit-rate for cold-but-reused prefixes. we should quantify hit-rate curve vs TTL.
PerfBot: quick simulated TTL sweep (approx): ttl=3600s -> hit=73.4% / mem=74.6GB; ttl=1800s -> hit=72.1% / mem=68.9GB; ttl=600s -> hit=69.0% / mem=61.3GB
Sam R: plotted hit-rate vs mem: roughly linear down to 20% hit-rate. marginal recovery per extra GB is diminishing after ~70GB.
Eli: suggestion: tiered caching: keep small hot prefixes in super-fast recycler slabs (e.g., 8MB slabs) with very low TTL, and larger cold prefixes in big slabs with longer TTL but lazy compaction. That might balance hit-rate for critical prefixes while bounding peak memory.
Maria (runtime): liking that. implementation notes: need two allocator classes per shard or a size-class map, metrics per tier, and a background migrator. also add per-prefix weight so we don't evict frequently-scored prefixes.
AJ: actionable checklist:
- run TTL sweep + slab-tier config on canary traffic (Maria)
- prototype background scavenger that moves slabs async (Eli)
- add per-prefix weight and size-aware eviction tests (Sam R)
- track tail-latency (p99) and p95 jitter (PerfBot)

Maria (runtime): I'll kick off canary tonight with 2-hour rolling window. copying config used below for record: 

```
kv_cache:
  shard_count: 64
  shard_workspace_cap: 32MB
  slab_recycler: true
  slab_tiers:
    - name: hot
      slab_size: 8MB
      ttl_seconds: 600
    - name: cold
      slab_size: 64MB
      ttl_seconds: 3600
  eviction_policy: size_aware
```

Sam R: please add the perf trace link when available, I'll run diff on p99/p95 and hit-rate per prefix histogram.
Maria (runtime): will do. if background scavenger looks stable we can iterate on donation thresholds. thanks all. :thumbsup:
AJ: nice work — excited to see the canary results.
PerfBot: scheduled canary run at 1768010800, will post summary when complete.
